lessons.title: Listen and speak: a counting rhyme
lessons.objective: Listen to, say and act a short rhyme, and retell a little story with gestures.
lessons.course:
A rhyme is a short poem with words that sound the same at the end: ball – wall, hop – stop.
We say it with rhythm and gestures, and we listen to our friends.

support.title: Say the Klassia rhyme
support.text:
One, two, kick the ball,
Three, four, by the wall,
Five, six, hop, hop, hop,
Seven, eight, now we stop!

lessons.model: The adult says the rhyme with gestures: kick, point to the wall, hop, then stop with arms open.
lessons.guided: Say the rhyme line by line after the adult, then all together with the gestures. Find the words that sound the same.
lessons.exercise: Which word sounds like “ball” in the rhyme?
lessons.remediation: Say the first two lines only, with the gestures.
lessons.transfer: Teach the rhyme to a brother, a sister or a friend.

practice.prompt: Listen to the rhyme and say it after the voice.
practice.listen: One, two, kick the ball. Three, four, by the wall. Five, six, hop, hop, hop. Seven, eight, now we stop!
practice.explanation: Say each line with its gesture.

practice.prompt: Match the words that sound the same.
practice.explanation: Rhyming words end with the same sound.

practice.prompt: Put the lines of the rhyme in order.
practice.explanation: The numbers help you find the order.

lessons.title: Read: longer words in parts
lessons.objective: Read words of two and three syllables by cutting them into parts.
lessons.course:
Long words have parts called syllables. We clap for each part: foot-ball (2), skip-ping (2), bi-cy-cle (3).
We read each part, then the whole word.
lessons.model: The adult claps and reads: “hop… scotch: hopscotch. We play hopscotch in the school yard.”
lessons.guided: Clap the parts of each word, then read it. Sort the words: two claps or three claps.
lessons.remediation: Clap two-part words only (football, skipping) before three-part words.
lessons.transfer: Clap the parts of the names of your friends.

practice.prompt: Put the parts in order to read the word.
How many parts in “football”?
Which word has three parts?

lessons.title: Write: short sentences (who does what)
lessons.objective: Write a short sentence with a subject, a verb and an object, starting with a capital letter and ending with a full stop.
lessons.course:
A short sentence says who does what: Tabi kicks the ball. Bih skips the rope.
It starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.

support.title: Copy with the adult
support.text:
Tabi kicks the ball.
Bih skips the rope.

lessons.model: The adult writes: “Neba throws the ball.” and points: “Who? Neba. Does what? throws. What? the ball.”
lessons.guided: Choose a name, an action and a thing from three boxes of cards. Build the sentence, read it, then write it.
lessons.exercise: Write a sentence: Ashu / plays / football.
lessons.remediation: Copy a model sentence first, then change only the name.
lessons.transfer: Write one sentence about the game you like.
lessons.materials: Cards with names, actions and things; pencil.

practice.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.
practice.explanation: Who? Bih. Does what? skips. What? the rope.

practice.prompt: Write the sentence: Tabi kicks the ball.
practice.explanation: Capital letter at the start, full stop at the end.

practice.prompt: What do we put at the end of a sentence?
practice.explanation: A sentence ends with a full stop.

lessons.title: Yesterday and today: here, there, now
lessons.objective: Say what happened yesterday with regular verbs in the simple past, and use adverbs of time and place.
lessons.course:
Today we play. Yesterday we played. For many verbs, we add ed to talk about the past: jump → jumped, kick → kicked.
Adverbs of time: now, today, yesterday. Adverbs of place: here, there.

support.title: Say with the adult
support.text:
Today I jump. Yesterday I jumped.
Come here! The ball is there.

lessons.model: The adult says: “Now I kick the ball. Yesterday I kicked the ball too.” Then points: “The ball is there. Bring it here.”
lessons.guided: Say what you do today, then what you did yesterday, adding ed. Play “here and there” with a ball.
lessons.remediation: Practise with three verbs only: play, jump, kick.
lessons.transfer: Tell an adult what you played yesterday.

practice.prompt: Add ed to talk about yesterday.
practice.text: Yesterday we jump[[ed]] and kick[[ed]] the ball.

practice.prompt: Which word tells about the past?
practice.explanation: Yesterday is the day before today.

practice.prompt: Complete: Come ___! (to the place where I am)
practice.explanation: Here is where I am; there is another place.

lessons.title: The table of 3
lessons.objective: Build the multiplication table of 3 and use it in games.
lessons.model: In a game, each team has 3 players. The adult counts: “1 team: 3 players. 2 teams: 6 players. 4 teams: 12 players.”
lessons.guided: Make groups of 3 stones. Say the table as you add a group each time.
lessons.remediation: Count in 3s with groups of objects: 3, 6, 9.
lessons.transfer: Count the legs of 3-legged stools in 3s.

practice.prompt: Complete the count in 3s.
4 teams of 3 players. How many players?

lessons.title: Tallies in 3s and telling the results
lessons.objective: Tally in 3s, collect the results of a game and present them orally.
lessons.course:
We can count tallies in 3s: 3, 6, 9, 12.
After a game, we collect the results in a table and say them: “Team A scored 9, team B scored 6. Team A won.”
lessons.model: The adult tallies points in a game of marbles in groups of 3 and announces the results aloud.
lessons.guided: Play a short game. Make a tally for each point. Count in 3s and say the results to the group.
lessons.remediation: Group the tally marks in 3s with a circle before counting.
lessons.transfer: Keep the score of a game with your friends using tallies.

practice.prompt: Team A has 3 groups of 3 points. How many points?
Team A: 9 points. Team B: 6 points. Which team won?
Say the results of the game in one sentence.
practice.answer: Team A scored 9 points and won.

lessons.title: Making shapes
lessons.objective: Construct triangles, squares, rectangles and circles with sticks, string and paper.
lessons.course: We can make shapes: a triangle with 3 sticks, a square with 4 equal sticks, a rectangle with 2 long and 2 short sticks. A circle is made with a string around a can.
lessons.model: The adult places 4 equal sticks: “4 equal sides: a square.” Then 2 long and 2 short: “a rectangle.”
lessons.guided: Use sticks of the same and different lengths to make each shape. Name each shape.
lessons.exercise: How many sticks do you need for a triangle?
lessons.remediation: Copy a shape drawn on paper by putting sticks on top of it.
lessons.transfer: Draw the shape of a hopscotch game on the ground.
lessons.materials: Sticks or straws, string, a tin.

practice.prompt: How many sides does a square have?
Match each shape with how we make it.
practice.answer: triangle: 3; square: 4 equal; rectangle: 2 long, 2 short.

practice.prompt: Draw a rectangle.
practice.answer: A shape with 2 long sides and 2 short sides.
practice.explanation: Opposite sides are the same length.

lessons.title: Problems about games
lessons.objective: Choose to add, take away or share to solve a simple problem.
lessons.course:
To solve a problem, read it, find what we know and what we look for, then choose: add (more), take away (less), share (equal parts).
Neba has 12 marbles. He wins 5. More marbles: we add. 12 + 5 = 17.
lessons.model: The adult reads a problem and thinks aloud: “She loses some: that is less. I take away.”
lessons.guided: Act out each problem with marbles, then write the operation.
lessons.exercise: Bih has 18 marbles. She loses 6. How many does she have now?
lessons.remediation: Act out the problem with objects before writing the numbers.
lessons.transfer: Make up a problem about a game you play.

practice.prompt: Tabi has 10 marbles. He wins 7 more. How many marbles now?
12 marbles shared equally between 2 friends. How many each?
Ekane had 9 balls and gave away 4. What do we do?
practice.explanation: He has less: we take away. 9 − 4 = 5.
